prompt: Greensboro buyer's agent Kevin learns from a contractor that the house his client is buying had a cracked foundation that was patched and hidden behind new drywall. The seller has not disclosed it, and the due diligence period is still open. What must Kevin do?

Stay silent, since disclosure is the seller's duty
Tell the buyer after the due diligence period ends

explanation: A buyer's agent must disclose to the client every material fact he learns, and a concealed foundation defect is a classic material latent defect that an inspection may miss. distractorExplanations.c: Delay defeats the purpose; the buyer needs the fact before due diligence ends, while she can still act on it.
distractorExplanations.d: The duty of disclosure runs first to Kevin's own client; withholding a material defect from her breaches his agency duties.

prompt: Ana, Ben, and Cara own a Wilmington beach cottage as tenants in common, one-third each. Ben dies, and his will leaves everything to his wife, Dee. How is the cottage owned after Ben's estate is settled?

options.text: Ana and Cara, one-half each, by survivorship
Ana and Cara, with Dee holding a life estate
Ana, Cara, and Dee as new joint tenants, one-third each
Ana, Cara, and Dee as tenants in common, a third each

explanation: Tenants in common have no right of survivorship. Each co-owner's undivided share passes at death by will or intestacy, so Ben's one-third goes through his estate to Dee. She becomes a tenant in common with Ana and Cara, holding an undivided one-third interest that she may sell or leave to her own heirs.

distractorExplanations.a: Survivorship belongs to joint tenancy; tenants in common pass their shares by will, so Ben's third goes to Dee.
distractorExplanations.b: The will gave Dee Ben's full one-third interest; nothing in a tenancy in common limits an heir to a life estate.
distractorExplanations.c: An heir does not become a joint tenant by inheritance; Dee takes Ben's share in the existing tenancy in common.

distractorExplanations.a: That is one point, the share the seller agreed to pay; the buyers still owe the other two points.

distractorExplanations.d: Charges all 3 points on the price, ignoring both the seller's point and the rule that points are based on the loan.
